newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger to speak to NZ First's Peters soon.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger to speak to NZ First's Peters soon.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Monday he expected to speak to New Zealand First leader Winston Peters "relatively soon" but no time had been set.
Bolger said he had not spoken to any party leaders on Monday in the wake of the inconclusive general election, which left New Zealand First holding the balance of power.
Party caucuses will meet on Tuesday. "We will discuss in caucus possible coalitions, possible minority governments and all the structures that go with that," Bolger told reporters.
Asked when he would talk to Peters, he said: "That's yet to be determined. I would expect to speak to Mr Peters relatively soon, but we haven't put that in train yet."
Bolger said he was not drawing any conclusions from comments by Peters' deputy Tau Henare.

Henare earlier described as a "bungle" his pre-election comment that he personally could not work with the conservative National Party unless it dumped Bolger, Finance Minister Bill Birch and Health Minister Jenny Shipley. However, he said it would be extremely difficult for him to do so.
Bolger was speaking after a cabinet meeting which he said had given thought to a "preliminary position" on coalitions.

New Zealand could end up with a centre-right or centre-left coalition depending on whether NZ First opts to go with National or Labour. Bolger has also not ruled out the possibility of a minority government with support from nine MPs from free-market Act New Zealand and the centrist United party.
Asked if he felt secure in his job, Bolger replied: "Absolutely." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
